Cair Paravel RuinsThe Chronicles of Narnia: Prince CaspianBack to Narnia. Apples first.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersCair Paravel applesRed and green apple slices with warm honey peanut butterHow to make it2 red apples2 green apples4 tbsp peanut butter2 tbsp honey1 pinch ground cinnamonSlice the apples and fan them on a board.Warm the peanut butter with honey until loose.Spoon into a bowl in the middle and dust the apples with cinnamon.Trumpkin's dwarf breadSelf-raising bread with rubbed in butter, scored and bakedHow to make it450g self-raising flour60g butter, for the dough1 pinch salt300ml full cream milk100g butter, to serveHeat the oven to 200°C. Rub the butter for the dough into the flour and salt.Mix in the milk with a knife until it just comes together.Shape into a round and score the top.Bake.Tear warm and serve with butter.Reepicheep's cheddar and chive sconesReepicheep, the bravest mouse in NarniaHow to make itAs written, serves 4Little scones packed with vintage cheddar and chives, baked tall and golden with a cheesy crust, split and spread with cold butter.Rub 60g cold butter into 350g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt and half a teaspoon mustard powder.Stir in 120g grated vintage cheddar and a handful of chopped chives, then 250ml milk to make a soft dough.Pat out 3cm thick and cut 12 small rounds.Brush with milk, top with 30g more cheese and bake at 220°C for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and golden.Serve warm with butter.Roasted chestnuts with sea saltPeter and Caspian, still arguing at the fire.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsAslan's How camp stewLamb shoulder simmered with pearl barley, carrots, leeks and rosemaryHow to make it1kg lamb shoulder, diced150g pearl barley3 carrots2 leeks2 sprigs of rosemary1.5 L water1 loaf crusty bread2 tbsp vegetable oilSlice the carrots and leeks.Brown the lamb in oil.Add the barley, vegetables, rosemary and water and simmer until the lamb is tender.Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread.Telmarine fennel roast pork loinMiraz's Telmarine castleHow to make itAs written, serves 4Pork loin rubbed with fennel seed and garlic, roasted at 200°C for an hour with apples and potatoes, sliced with pan juices.Score the skin of a 1.5kg boneless pork loin and pat dry.Crush 2 tsp fennel seeds with 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp salt and pepper and rub into the meat, then rub the skin with oil and salt.Roast at 220°C for 25 minutes, then 180°C for 40 minutes.Add 800g potatoes in chunks for the last 60 minutes and 4 halved apples for the last 30.Rest 10 minutes, slice and spoon over the pan juices.SweetsNarnian apple crumbleCinnamon green apples under an oat crumbleHow to make it5 green apples30g butter, for the apples1 tsp ground cinnamon70g butter, for the topping100g rolled oats100g plain flour80g brown sugar500ml custardPeel and slice the apples.Melt the butter for the apples in a pan, add the apples and cinnamon and cook, then spoon into a dish.Rub the topping butter into the oats, flour and sugar and scatter over.Bake at 180°C.Warm the custard and serve over the crumble.DrinksStation platform malted hot chocolateMilk whisked with dark chocolate, malt powder and brown sugarHow to make it1 L full cream milk120g dark chocolate4 tbsp malted milk powder1 tbsp brown sugar1 can whipped cream1 pinch malted milk powder, to finishChop the chocolate.Heat the milk until steaming.Whisk in the chocolate, malted milk powder and sugar until smooth and frothy.Pour into mugs and top with cream and a pinch of malt.
